reclassified.note: All four pilot discards were classifier artifacts: two cross-call cwd, one output-flag write, one a JS arrow read as a redirect.

effortMethod: Effort is summarised as the MEDIAN over runs, not the mean: one run that hits its turn cap would otherwise move an arm on its own. Each comparison is PAIRED BY TASK — per task, the difference of the two arms' medians, and that difference as a fraction of the REFERENCE arm's median, since a task's turn count is set by the task. The stripped arm's reference is the tarball it was cut from, not the baseline: against a build from another commit, losing the docs and changing the library would be one effect. The aggregate is the mean of those per-task values, with a 95% percentile bootstrap over TASKS (2000 resamples, seeded per arm/reference/metric — so the same runs.jsonl always prints the same interval, and the metric rows are independent draws rather than one draw repeated) and an exact two-sided sign test on the per-task signs. The bootstrap treats the tasks as the sample: it answers 'would another set of tasks like these show the same difference', which is the question a campaign of a handful of tasks can ask. The A/A pair is the noise floor: whatever separates the same tarball under two labels is what run-to-run wobble looks like here, and an effect smaller than that is not an effect.

gate.label: Pilot gate
reasons: (a) stripped arm 100.0% is not below both references (100.0%, 100.0%) by more than the A/A gap 0.0% and at least 17.0%: the eval may not see documentation
(c) 6 of 6 task(s) at floor or ceiling on solved, replace from reserve: even-spacing, riverbank, road-props, settlement-roads, species-mix, trees-on-hills

fix: make the stripped arm cost something — harder tasks (limb (c) names the saturated ones), or a stronger strip set — because the arms did not separate; replace the floor/ceiling task(s) from the reserve and re-run

caveat: n = 18 runs per arm. A Wilson interval this wide detects only large effects; pass rates are not significance tests, and the gate is a go/stop rule, not a hypothesis test.
